record.original_question: Consider a semi-algebraic set in R^k defined by l quadratic inequalities. Can the number of connected components of such a set be computed by an algorithm with complexity k^O(l), or even k^O(l^2), rather than the currently best known k^(2^O(l)) type bound coming from the available all-Betti-number methods? Equivalently, is there a substantially more efficient algorithm for counting connected components in the quadratic case than the general-purpose approach currently provides?

evidence.quote: More Efficient Algorithms for Computing the Number of Connected Components in the Quadratic Case ? For semi-algebraic sets in R^k defined by l quadratic inequalities, there are algorithms for deciding emptiness, as well as computing sample points in every connected component whose complexity is bounded by k^O(l) [3, 45]. We also have an algorithm [9] for computing the Euler-Poincare characteristic of such sets whose complexity is k^O(l).

However, the best known algorithm for computing the number of connected components of such sets has complexity k^(2^O(l)) (as a special case of the algorithm for computing all the Betti numbers given in Theorem 2.6). This raises the question whether there exists a more efficient algorithm with complexity k^O(l) or even k^O(l^2) for counting the number of connected components of such sets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k,\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $P_1,\dots,P_\ell \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$ be polynomials each of degree at most $2$. Consider a semi-algebraic set
$$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$$
defined by a Boolean combination of the sign conditions $\{P_i \,\square\, 0 : 1 \le i \le \ell,\ \square \in \{<,=,>\}\}$ (in particular, sets defined by conjunctions of $\ell$ quadratic inequalities $P_i \le 0$).

Currently:
- Algorithms are known that decide emptiness of $S$ and compute a set of sample points meeting every connected component of $S$ in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
- The Euler–Poincaré characteristic $\chi(S)$ can be computed in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
- The number $b_0(S)$ of connected components of $S$ can be computed by specializing general algorithms for all Betti numbers, which run in time $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$.

Question. Does there exist an algorithm that, given the polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_\ell$ as input (in a standard bit-cost or arithmetic complexity model over an ordered field where the relevant arithmetic is performed exactly), outputs the number $b_0(S)$ of connected components of $S$ in time bounded by $k^{O(\ell)}$, or at least by $k^{O(\ell^2)}$, thereby substantially improving on the current $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$ bound?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on algorithms for semi-algebraic sets defined by quadratic inequalities (Basu and coauthors) achieves polynomial-time algorithms for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic and for the top few Betti numbers, but the best known complexity for computing the full count of connected components of such sets remains $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$, inherited from the all-Betti-numbers algorithm. Moreover, exact counting of connected components in the quadratic case is known to be #P-hard, but no algorithm with complexity $k^{O(\ell)}$ or $k^{O(\ell^2)}$ has been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Computing the Top Betti Numbers of Semi-algebraic Sets Defined by Quadratic Inequalities in Polynomial Time
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the top ℓ Betti numbers in polynomial time; complexity for general Betti numbers (and hence b_0 via that route) is k^{2^{O(ℓ)}}.
status_evidence.claim: Top Betti numbers solved in polynomial time; the general number-of-components bound k^{2^{O(ℓ)}} not improved.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology (Basu survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing complexity bounds k^{O(ℓ)} for emptiness and Euler characteristic, and k^{2^{O(ℓ)}} for all Betti numbers including b_0 in the quadratic case.
status_evidence.claim: Current best general bound for computing number of connected components in the quadratic case is k^{2^{O(ℓ)}}.

status_evidence.title: Computing the Top Betti Numbers of Semialgebraic Sets Defined by Quadratic Inequalities (quadstoc.pdf)
status_evidence.snippet: Counting connected components for sets defined by quadratic inequalities is #P-hard, indicating that a fully polynomial algorithm is unlikely, but no improved k^{O(ℓ)} algorithm is given.
status_evidence.claim: #P-hardness suggests difficulty, but a substantially improved algorithm has not been ruled out within the k^{O(ℓ^2)} regime.
